properties.name: Tigris & Euphrates Confluence
properties.subtitle: Al-Qurnah, Basra Governorate, Iraq
properties.claim: The four-river description of Eden in Genesis is matched to this confluence, and the garden read as an off-world genetics facility.
properties.context: Genesis names Tigris, Euphrates, Pishon and Gihon; the latter two are unidentified, and proposals range from the Karun and Wadi al-Batin to the Nile. The alluvium here has shifted substantially since antiquity, and the Shatt al-Arab itself is a late formation — which is why no fixed location can be derived from the text.
properties.summary: The Shatt al-Arab (Arabic: شط العرب, lit. 'River of the Arabs') is a river about 200 kilometres (120 mi) in length that is formed at the confluence of the Euphrates and Tigris rivers in the town of al-Qurnah in the Basra Governorate of southern Iraq. The southern end of the river constitutes the Iran–Iraq border down to its mouth, where it discharges into the Persian Gulf.
